answer: The verifier mandates 1,000 unique location proofs to anchor each agent within a specific dune to ensure identity uniqueness. Each node must provide a signed receipt of its spatial signal, which the issuer validates against a synchronized grove of relays. The verifier replicates any signal failure by re-running the timing logs; if overlap occurs, the identity is purged. An honest agent incurs linear travel costs to reach base stations, while an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes faces the cost of physical infrastructure. The nectar of this system is its falsifiable proof-of-transit geometry.
